args.message: Fix FIN-212: use ROUND_HALF_EVEN for banker's rounding in round_money

args.head: fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix FIN-212: implement banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money
args.body:
The nightly build failed because tests/test_money.py expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` was quantizing with ROUND_HALF_UP.

Changes:
- Import ROUND_HALF_EVEN instead of ROUND_HALF_UP in src/money.py.
- round_money() now quantizes with rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN as its docstring already specified.

CI run ci-0001 on this branch passed.

Done. Here's a summary:

**Problem:** `src/money.py`'s `round_money()` was quantizing with `ROUND_HALF_UP` even though its docstring (and tests, per FIN-212) require banker's rounding — causing `tests/test_money.py` to fail in the nightly build.

**Fix:** Created branch `fix/fin-212-bankers-rounding` and committed the one-line-ish fix: import and use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` in `amount.quantize(Decimal("0.01"), rounding=ROUND_HALF_EVEN)`.

**CI:** Triggered a run (`ci-0001`) on the branch — it passed.

**PR:** Opened [PR #101](https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101) against `main` with review requested from **alex**. (The first PR attempt hit a transient 503, so I retried it; only one PR exists.)

I did not merge anything into main, per policy — the PR is waiting on alex's code-owner approval.
